reclamation.why: Only goods qualify. Three deliveries fall inside the 45-day pre-petition window (window opens 2026-01-24, petition 2026-03-10): MS-7740 steel coil received 2026-02-04 (unpaid balance 25,600), MS-7788 structural steel received 2026-02-20 (41,300), MS-7815 steel coil received 2026-03-04 (36,800) = 103,700 of goods. MS-7802 (freight & handling) and MS-7819 (on-site cutting services) are not 'goods'. MS-7701 (received 2026-01-14) is outside the 45-day window and was paid. No written demand has been served yet. For each of the three, the 45-days-after-receipt date (2026-03-21, 2026-04-06, 2026-04-18) expires after commencement, so the controlling deadline is 20 days after the petition: 2026-03-30 (11 days from today). Availability is therefore real but of little cash value: reclamation is subject to prior liens, here the DIP lender's blanket lien, so treat it as negotiation leverage for the critical-vendor discussion, not as a recovery channel (library/bc_503b9_546c.md). Practical value also depends on the goods being traceable in Redwood's inventory, which is not established in the file.

ordinary_course_defense.reasoning: 90-day window opens 2025-12-10. Four payments fall inside: 2025-12-18 51,000 (45 days after invoice, ACH), 2026-01-22 44,000 (43 days, ACH), 2026-02-10 48,200 (29 days, ACH), 2026-02-27 36,800 (25 days, WIRE demanded by Mesa's credit manager) = 180,000. PROTECTED 95,000 = 51,000 + 44,000: both fit the parties' 12-month history (43-47 days after invoice, all ACH) and both pre-date or match the historical net-45 terms. EXPOSED 85,000 = 48,200 + 36,800: both were made after Mesa's credit department unilaterally cut terms to NET 15 and demanded the oldest open invoice first (email dated 2026-01-20), and the Feb 27 item was a wire on demand - the library states that payments under shortened terms, pressure, or unusual methods compared with the parties' history generally fall outside 547(c)(2)(A) (library/bc_547.md). CLIENT ADMISSIONS CORROBORATE THE EXPOSED SPLIT: Lori (credit manager, client answer 2026-03-19) says 'In January I cut them to net-15 and made them pay the oldest invoice before I'd ship' (the 2026-02-10 ACH) and for the 2026-02-27 wire 'I told them no steel until it hit our account.' The earlier sensitivity that the 2026-02-10 ACH might be held ordinary is now unlikely - Mesa's own witness ties both payments to the shortened terms and to shipping conditions. 547(c)(2)(B) 'ordinary business terms' (industry benchmark) remains unproven - the client has no industry-terms evidence - and 547(g) puts the burden on Mesa as the defending creditor. NEW ISSUE FROM THE SAME ADMISSIONS: because Mesa itself conditioned each new shipment on prior payment, a court could treat the 48,200 and 36,800 payments as otherwise unavoidable transfers made 'on account of' the later new value, eroding the 99,400 new-value credit; the library states the (c)(4) text but not this application, so that reading is labelled UNVERIFIED. Exposure range: 0 (full new-value credit allowed) to 85,000 ceiling; 63,700 mid-case if 20-day goods cannot also count as new value (also unresolved on the library). Insolvency (§547(b)(3)) is presumed inside the 90 days under §547(f), and §547(b)(5) 'more than in a chapter 7' is likely satisfied for a trade creditor. See workpapers_calculations.md for the arithmetic.

stay_violations: 2026-03-12 'FINAL NOTICE - pay $210,000 within 5 days or we refer to collections' letter, mailed and emailed 2 days after the 2026-03-10 petition: an act to collect a pre-petition claim, stayed by §362(a)(6); the library states dunning letters after the petition are acts to collect (library/bc_362.md). The demand also overstated the open balance: 210,000 invoiced since 2026-01-12 less 85,000 already paid = 125,000, so Mesa demanded 85,000 that had already been paid. Client explanation (Frank, 2026-03-19): the letter was generated automatically by Mesa's dunning system, which sends final notices to every account 30 days late. That may help on the undefined 'willful' element but does not undo the act, and the system will keep firing - suppress the account today and check whether later automated notices also went out post-petition.

2026-03-15 collection call to Redwood AP, made after Redwood's representative stated on that same call that a Chapter 11 had been filed; the recorded reply 'that's not our problem, you owe us' is direct evidence that collection staff pushed a demand notwithstanding notice of the case. Note: that reply was Mesa's own AR clerk speaking - the file contains no assertion by Redwood of any claim against Mesa, so Form 410's 'subject to offset' box has nothing behind it yet. Client adds (Frank): Lori called twice - the log records only one call; find the phone records for the second call and treat it as a probable further post-petition contact pending verification.

2026-03-18 email to Redwood's CFO threatening to 'hold all future shipments and report to credit bureaus' - the library expressly lists threats to report to credit bureaus after the petition as acts to collect; the shipment threat was tied to pre-petition payment, so it reads as collection leverage rather than a legitimate prospective credit decision.

Exposure: §362(k) gives actual damages, costs and attorneys' fees, and punitive damages in appropriate circumstances, for willful violations; the library notes courts also sanction corporate creditors under §105. Redwood is a corporation, so the §105 sanction route matters more here than §362(k)'s 'individual' language. The library does not define 'willful', so whether the 2026-03-12 letter (sent before it is established that Mesa knew of the filing) is 'willful' is unverified; the 2026-03-15 and 2026-03-18 acts, made after notice of the filing, carry the highest risk.

Also stayed and not yet done but must not be done without relief from stay: setoff of pre-petition mutual debts (§553; library/bc_502d_setoff.md), applying deposits or credit balances against the pre-petition balance, reporting Redwood to credit bureaus, filing a lien, and accepting any payment of pre-petition invoices.
immediate_actions: TODAY: written stand-down to the whole AR/credit team - no letters, calls, emails, credit-bureau reporting, lien filings, deposit offsets or demands of any kind against Redwood; all contact routes through counsel to Redwood's counsel. Keep the instruction and its distribution list; it is the mitigation record if a stay-violation motion follows (library/bc_362.md).
TODAY: litigation hold on all Redwood account records, the 2026-01-20 terms email, wire/ACH records and the collection log. Do not delete or 'correct' the collection log.

By 2026-03-30: serve a written §546(c) reclamation demand on Redwood and its counsel for MS-7740, MS-7788 and MS-7815. This is a hard deadline (20 days after the petition) and it is cheap; expect little cash because the DIP lender's blanket lien primes the right (library/bc_503b9_546c.md).

TODAY: suppress the Redwood account in the automated dunning/collections system. Frank confirms the 2026-03-12 final notice was auto-generated for any account 30 days late, and this account is 40+ days late, so the system will send more notices unless suppressed. Confirm today whether any automated notice, statement or credit-bureau report went out after 2026-03-10; each one is a separate act to collect (library/bc_362.md).

By 2026-04-02: respond - through counsel - to Redwood's counsel, who has already asked whether Mesa would keep supplying on normal terms if the old invoices are paid (Frank answered 'pay first' and did not know a critical-vendor motion was pending). That proposal is essentially the critical-vendor bargain: under the practice note the debtor may pay pre-petition claims of essential vendors who agree to customary trade terms for the case, subject to court approval; 'pay first before we ship' cuts against the terms the court expects (library/critical_vendor_practice.md; Dkt. 44, hearing 2026-04-02). Mesa's leverage is the 78,100 administrative claim plus the reclamation demand; the offsetting risk is Mesa's preference exposure up to 85,000. All dialogue with Redwood must now run lawyer-to-lawyer.

File the §503(b)(9) request for 78,100 (MS-7788 41,300 + MS-7815 36,800) as an administrative expense, separately from the general unsecured claim. The client holds no bar-date order or 503(b)(9) procedure beyond the notice, so counsel must obtain the operative order from the claims agent/docket; the library says the request is made by motion or per the bar-date order, so protect the position with a stand-alone §503(b)(9) motion rather than relying on a form checkbox (library/frbp_3002_3003.md). Flag the proof risk: Mesa can produce no signed delivery receipts, and MS-7788 sits only 2 days inside the 20-day window on the spreadsheet date, so 41,300 of the administrative classification depends on the 2026-02-20 receipt date surviving challenge.

File Official Form 410 for 125,000 total, with the 78,100 administrative portion separately stated, no later than 2026-06-11 at 5:00 p.m. Mountain Time by e-filing with the claims agent; a late claim is barred absent excusable neglect and costs Mesa its voting and distribution rights (library/frbp_3002_3003.md; documents/notice_of_commencement_and_bar_date.pdf).

Attend the creditors' meeting scheduled for 2026-04-21, 10:00 a.m. Mountain (telephonic) - the case notice calls it the Meeting of Creditors held under section 341, a fact taken from the notice, not a library citation - and confirm the bar-date mechanics; the notice in the file is internally inconsistent (it is dated 2026-04-02, a future date), so get the operative order (see QUESTIONS.md).

Quantify and reserve for preference exposure before asserting the claim aggressively: Mesa may be liable for up to 85,000 of the 180,000 received in the 90 days; the new-value defense of 99,400 should reduce that to about zero, but Lori's admissions that shipments were conditioned on prior payment put the new-value credit in issue (see preference reasoning - the point is unresolved and not covered in the library, labelled unverified). Recommended reserve: 85,000 (the ceiling) until the new-value question is settled; 63,700 is the mid-case if only the 20-day-goods overlap fails. Under §502(d) an unpaid preference liability can cause Mesa's whole 125,000 claim to be disallowed until it is paid (library/bc_547.md, library/bc_502d_setoff.md).

Do not accept any payment from Redwood on pre-petition invoices: it would be an unauthorized transfer, it can be unwound, and it creates a fresh avoidable transfer. Any post-petition shipments must be on current, court-approved terms (the library does not cover payment for post-petition deliveries - treat that as unverified and confirm with debtor's counsel and the DIP lender's order).
